name: PF-08653945
lead: PF-08653945, formerly MET-233i, is an investigational amylin analogue for weight management, now developed by Pfizer after its acquisition of Metsera. It is not approved.[2] Its appearance relevance is through fat loss: amylin analogues aim to reduce appetite and body weight, which people pursue for a leaner body and face.

Pfizer describes MET-233i as a monthly amylin analogue candidate in Phase 1 development, being evaluated alone and in combination with the incretin candidate MET-097i; initial Phase 1 results were presented at the 61st EASD Annual Meeting on 17 September 2025, and the acquisition was announced on 22 September 2025.[2]
It belongs to the amylin analogue class, which a 2026 narrative review describes as an emerging therapeutic approach to obesity complementing incretin-based drugs.[1]

paras: Metsera developed MET-233i; Pfizer announced in September 2025 that it would acquire the company. Pfizer's release lists MET-233i as a monthly amylin analogue in Phase 1, studied as monotherapy and combined with MET-097i.[2]

No peer-reviewed results for PF-08653945 have been located. Initial Phase 1 results of MET-233i were presented at the EASD meeting in September 2025.[2] A 2026 review covers amylin-based therapies in obesity more broadly, including early-phase trials of the class.[1]

timeline.event: Initial Phase 1 results for MET-233i presented at EASD (17 September); Pfizer announces Metsera acquisition (22 September).[2]

quick.overview:
PF-08653945 is an experimental amylin analogue being developed for weight loss. No trials or results were found for it specifically.

Amylin analogues are a drug class reviewed in 2026 as a possible next step after GLP-1 drugs.
quick.mechanism: Amylin analogues mimic a pancreatic hormone involved in satiety and slowing of digestion.
quick.risks: Human safety data for this compound are not public. It is unapproved and not legitimately available.

chain: Mimics amylin, a hormone involved in satiety
angle.text: Amylin analogues act on fullness and digestion to lower body weight. People interested in leaner bodies and faces follow the class as a possible next step beyond GLP-1 drugs.
